title: Scientists Found 1,121 New Ocean Species This Year — And That's Still Basically Nothing
youtube_description:
We just found over a thousand new species living in our own oceans. And it barely made a dent.

Between April 2025 and March 2026, the Ocean Census — a partnership between the Nippon Foundation, Nekton, JAMSTEC, CSIRO and the Schmidt Ocean Institute — ran 13 expeditions and 9 discovery workshops and came back with 1,121 new marine species. Not all of them were hiding in the deep: one new species was found off Timor-Leste in water only one to five metres deep, proof that you don't need a submarine to find something science has never seen.

Others were stranger. A brand new species of ghost shark was found living 800 metres down in Australia's Coral Sea Marine Park. Off Japan, researchers found a worm living inside a glass sponge on a seamount, 790 metres down — a species nobody had catalogued before. And in a sea cave off Marseille, one of the most heavily studied coastlines on Earth, a new shrimp species had been there the whole time.

Here's the number that actually matters: marine biologists estimate up to 90% of ocean species remain undiscovered. 1,121 new species in a year sounds huge — and it's still just the tip of the iceberg.
